Harbor lanterns

From Example Wiki

Harbor lanterns are paper lights that fishing towns float on the water at the end of the autumn season. Each household folds a lantern, writes a wish on the base and sets it on the tide after dusk, and the harbor master records how many reach the breakwater.

History

[edit]

The custom began as a way to mark safe returns after the last long voyage of the year. Early lanterns used oiled paper over a reed frame, and families reused the frames for several seasons before the town switched to folded card that dissolves in salt water.

Town records describe a quiet evening, with the lanterns released from the north quay in small groups so that the boats can count them. Volunteers collect any that wash back onto the beach the following morning and log them with the date and the wind direction.

Materials

  • Folded card that softens in salt water
  • A short beeswax candle in a clay cup
  • Plant dye for the written wish
